notes.text: The branch — The kings they had hitherto had of the line of David, were most of them unrighteous men, but God promises that after the captivity, they should have a branch of David who would execute judgment and righteousness in the land, for the protection and government of those that feared him.

Saved — It is the opinion of some that a spiritual salvation and security is promised under these expressions, but by the most and best interpreters, a temporal salvation. This was typical of that spiritual and eternal salvation which is promised to the true Israel of God; as their rest in Canaan typified that rest which remaineth for the people of God. The Lord our righteousness - There is no such name any where given, either to the Jewish or Christian church, as the Lord our righteousness, but the full import of that name is spoken of Christ, Isaiah xlv, 23, which text is applied to Christ, Rom. xiv, 11 Phil ii, 10.

glossa.text: *To the house of Israel:* Of whom Isaias: there shall be in the last days the mountain of the house of the Lord prepared on the top of the mountains, etc.

notes.text: Ashamed — Disappointed of my hope.
Cause — Without any provocation of mine.
Teach — Teach me my duty, and cause me to keep close to it, notwithstanding all temptations.
Upright — Holy and true, in all his declarations and offers of mercy to sinners. Therefore - He will not be wanting to such poor sinners as I am, but will guide them into the way of life and peace.
The meek — Such as meekly submit themselves to God, and are desirous to be directed and governed by him. Judgment - In the paths of judgment, in the right way.
Paths — All the dealings of God with them, yea even those that are afflictive, are done in kindness and faithfulness to them.

glossa.text:
*Unto the end.* ((Hier.)) Here the penitent who has been scourged is set before the rest, lest they murmur in adversities: he who, having had the trial in himself, coaxes through mercy and terrifies through justice.

 *To thee, O Lord, have I lifted up.* ((AUG.)) A psalm against the adversities of the world, etc., *as far as* who not through all, the less perfect.

((CASS.)) First he asks to be taught the ways of the Lord, because he is raised up toward God.

((ID.)) Toward the contemplating of thee; he easily despises earthly things who beholds things divine.

*I trust.* ((ID.)) Having had trial of my own weakness in evils, I shall not blush because of my enemies.

*Neither let my enemies laugh at me:* and I am sure that he deceives none that endures patiently.

*In vain.* ((ID.)) Because all things are vain and unfruitful which are alien from God.

*Shew me thy ways, O Lord.* ((CASS.)) The ways are of the order of life, etc., *as far as: Direct,* belongs to life, *teach* to knowledge.

*Teach.* ((AUG.)) Truth itself, that I may understand what I believe, because I have endured; and if this suffices not: *Remember.*

*God my saviour.* ((CASS.)) There are two things which make men good, that we believe God our saviour, and that we patiently await his retribution.

*Remember.* ((ID.)) Of former sins and of those which are daily done, he prays through the mercy shewn to the ancients, and because he fears a true judge.

*Of thy tender mercies.* Compassion is properly in the shewing forth of good things.

*Which are from of old.* ((AUG.)) That is, they are from the beginning of the world: therefore let him not fail in me.

*Sins.* ((CASS.)) They are when the way of equity is forsaken.

*Of my youth.* Not for age, but for the rashness of headlong haste, which is then, when the heat of the mind exceeds moderation.

*Ignorances.* We do those things which we do not know to be evil. Or the sins of ignorance in little ones, who are held at any rate by original sin.

((HIER.)) Of my youth. Before I went out of the house of my wicked father.

*Remember me, thou.* ((AUG.)) Whose work it is to have mercy and to forgive sins.

*According to thy mercy.* That is, thy mercy is ample. Mercy is toward the wretched, goodness toward any whatsoever. But God does good both when implored by the wretched, and when led by his goodness: none is good but God.

*Sweet.* ((ID.)) Because he forgives all former things, where grace is without merits.

*Right.* Because after mercy, etc., *as far as Sweet,* because he gives sweet things; *right,* because he corrects.

*Therefore.* ((CASS.)) Because he is sweet and right; not out of cruelty, but out of kindness.

*In the way.* That is, faith, or the precepts of God. Or in the way of this life, where one must live rightly, he will give a law.

*In judgment.* While he punishes, he will direct to better things. But let them be meek who are corrected: for from wild beasts they are tamed, that they may bear it. For if they are mild, that is, of a gentle mind, as though having this by nature: he will teach them the precepts for the neglect of which came the scourges.

*Mercy and truth.* ((AUG.)) But what ways he will teach, etc., *as far as* and then he guards against the severity of the judge.

*Testament.* ((CASS.)) The New, which is excellently called a Testament, where there is a clear and certain promise of an inheritance, which is confirmed by death also.

*And the Testament.* Of the old law, where the Prophets were witnesses of the promises.

notes.text: And perfect that which is wanting in your faith — So St. Paul did not know that "they who are once upon the rock no longer need to be taught by man."
Direct our way — This prayer is addressed to Christ, as well as to the Father.
With all his, Christ's, saints — Both angels and men.

glossa.text: *For what thanksgiving,* etc. For there is nothing so worthy as could suffice for the recompense of the salvation obtained for the Gentiles.

*Without complaint.* That you complain not of evils, or that you be so innocent that no one can complain of you; and that you may also be. *In holiness.* That is, existing thereby before God in the consummation of the virtues, not for the sight of men.

notes.text: And there shall be — Before the great day, which was typified by the destruction of Jerusalem: signs - Different from those mentioned in ver. 11. Matt. xxiv, 29; Mark xiii, 24.

Now when these things — Mentioned ver. 8, 10, &c., begin to come to pass, look up with firm faith, and lift up your heads with joy: for your redemption out of many troubles draweth nigh, by God's destroying your implacable enemies.
Behold the fig tree and all the trees — Christ spake this in the spring, just before the passover; when all the trees were budding on the Mount of Olives, where they then were.
Ye know of yourselves — Though none teach you.
The kingdom of God is nigh — The destruction of the Jewish city, temple, and religion, to make way for the advancement of my kingdom.
Till all things be effected — All that has been spoken of the destruction of Jerusalem, to which the question, ver. 7, relates: and which is treated of from ver. 8-24.

Take heed, lest at any time your hearts be overloaded with gluttony and drunkenness — And was there need to warn the apostles themselves against such sins as these? Then surely there is reason to warn even strong Christians against the very grossest sins. Neither are we wise, if we think ourselves out of the reach of any sin: and so that day - Of judgment or of death, come upon you, even you that are not of this world-Unawares. Matt. xxiv, 42; Mark xiii, 33; Luke xii, 35.
That sit — Careless and at ease.

Watch ye therefore — This is the general conclusion of all that precedes. That ye may be counted worthy - This word sometimes signifies an honour conferred on a person, as when the apostles are said to be counted worthy to suffer shame for Christ, Acts v, 41. Sometimes meet or becoming: as when John the Baptist exhorts, to bring fruits worthy of repentance, chap. iii, 8. And so to be counted worthy to escape, is to have the honour of it, and to be fitted or prepared for it. To stand - With joy and triumph: not to fall before him as his enemies.

glossa.text: *And there shall be signs.* These things are of his coming itself, when all the virgins, wise and foolish, roused by an unwonted cry, trim their lamps, that is, count over their works with themselves, for which with the greatest fear they await the now impending outcome of the eternal decision. As the last judgment draws near, the sound of the sea and of the waves is confounded, and the round world is stained with husbandmen pressing on every side; the greatest lights of heaven, their rays struck with a new horror, veil their troubled face, because, as their own end draws near, the elements as if in dread waver and roar.

*And then they shall see.* Him whom, set in humility, they would not hear, so that they may then feel his power the more strictly, the more that now they do not incline their hearts to his patience. But because these things were said against the reprobate, he presently subjoins matter for the consolation of the elect.

*But when these things begin to come to pass.* That is, when the plagues grow thick, when the terror of the judgment is shown by the shaking of the powers. *Lift up your heads.* Gladden your hearts, because, while the world to which you are not friends is being ended, the redemption which you seek is at hand. But that the world ought to be despised is made plain by a provident comparison.

*See the fig tree.* He compares the kingdom of God to summer, because then the clouds of our sorrow shall pass away, and the days of eternal life shall shine under the brightness of the sun. For as from the fruit of the trees the nearness of summer is known, so also from the ruin of the world the kingdom of God is known to be near. From these words it is shown that the fruit of the world is ruin. For it grows to this end, that it may fall; it buds to this end, that whatsoever it shall have budded it may consume with disasters.

*Heaven and earth.* Nothing in the nature of bodies is more lasting than heaven and earth. Nothing passes more swiftly than speech. Words, so long as they are unfinished, are not words; if they be finished, they now are not at all: for they cannot be finished save by passing away. He says therefore: *Heaven and earth shall pass away.* As if he said: Everything that with you is lasting and without change is not lasting unto eternity, and everything that with me is seen to pass is held fixed and without passing, because my speech, which passes, expresses abiding judgments. *But my words shall not pass away.* And since my words are thus without doubt to be fulfilled, see that, against the attestation of my words, you be not given over to surfeiting and drunkenness and the cares of this world, as certain men will be in the time of the impending judgment: of whom it is said: *When they shall say: Peace and security, sudden destruction shall come upon them ((I Thess. V))*.

hymns.title: From Jesse's root a branch shall grow: God's covenant shall be fulfilled
Walk in the light of God's counsel
The Lord comes, the Lord comes
In the bulb there is a flower
Lead on, O cloud of Presence
Where cross the crowded ways of life

praise.title: Lo, How a Rose E'er Blooming
Just a Closer Walk with Thee

echoes.attribution: Catena, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wilson Pruitt / Wroot Press)

echoes.text: What will I give to Yahweh for all his benefits toward me?
echoes.note: Paul's overflowing "what thanksgiving can we render again to God for you" echoes the psalmist's "What shall I render to the LORD for all his benefits toward me?" Both pose the rhetorical question of an adequate return of gratitude to God for received good, framed as thanksgiving rendered before God.

echoes.text: You shall flee by the valley of my mountains; for the valley of the mountains shall reach to Azel; yes, you shall flee, just like you fled from before the earthquake in the days of Uzziah king of Judah. Yahweh my God will come, and all the holy ones with you./f + Septuagint reads “him” instead of “you”./f*
echoes.note: "At the coming of our Lord Jesus with all his saints" closely reproduces Zechariah's "the LORD my God will come, and all the holy ones with him," a key text for the eschatological advent accompanied by the heavenly host. Paul applies the prophecy of the Lord's theophanic arrival with his holy ones directly to the parousia of Jesus.

echoes.text: He said, “Yahweh came from Sinai, and rose from Seir to them. He shone from Mount Paran. He came from the ten thousands of holy ones. At his right hand was a fiery law for them.
echoes.note: The advent of the Lord "with all his saints/holy ones" draws on the Sinai theophany where the LORD "came with myriads of holy ones," the foundational image of God arriving attended by his angelic host. The same verse stands behind the developed expectation of the divine coming surrounded by the holy ones.

echoes.text: A fiery stream issued and came out from before him: thousands of thousands ministered to him, and ten thousand times ten thousand stood before him: the judgment was set, and the books were opened.
echoes.note: The myriads of "holy ones" attending the Lord's coming evoke Daniel's throne vision, where thousands of thousands serve and ten thousand times ten thousand stand before the Ancient of Days. This apocalyptic court of attendants feeds the picture of Jesus arriving with all his holy ones.

echoes.text: The heavens will praise your wonders, Yahweh; your faithfulness also in the assembly of the holy ones. For who in the skies can be compared to Yahweh? Who among the sons of the heavenly beings is like Yahweh, a very awesome God in the council of the holy ones, to be feared above all those who are around him?
echoes.note: "All his saints" recalls the heavenly "assembly of the holy ones" who praise and surround the LORD, the council of holy ones before whom God is feared. Paul's holy retinue at the parousia shares this picture of the angelic congregation accompanying the divine presence.

echoes.text: In all your ways acknowledge him, and he will make your paths straight.
echoes.note: The prayer that God "direct our way to you" (kateuthynai) uses the Septuagintal vocabulary of God making straight one's paths, as in "he will direct your paths." The petition entrusts the missionaries' route to divine guidance in the manner of the wisdom tradition.

echoes.text: The chariots of God are tens of thousands and thousands of thousands. The Lord is among them, from Sinai, into the sanctuary.
echoes.note: The Lord coming "with all his saints" faintly recalls the chariots of God, "twice ten thousand, thousands upon thousands," the LORD among them as at Sinai. The motif of God advancing amid innumerable heavenly hosts overlaps with the parousia escort.

echoes.text: [source text not in the World English Bible]
echoes.note: The coming of the Lord "with all his holy ones" parallels the Enochic oracle that "the Lord will come with his holy myriads to execute judgment," itself an expansion of Deuteronomy 33:2. This pseudepigraphal text (cited in Jude 14-15) attests the same first-century expectation of the Lord's advent attended by his holy ones that Paul invokes.

echoes.text: When Abram was ninety-nine years old, Yahweh appeared to Abram, and said to him, “I am God Almighty. Walk before me, and be blameless.
echoes.note: The goal that God "establish your hearts blameless in holiness before our God" echoes the covenantal charge to "walk before me and be blameless." The pairing of blamelessness with standing before God recalls the patriarchal call to integrity in the divine presence.

echoes.text: His heart is established. He will not be afraid in the end when he sees his adversaries.
echoes.note: "Establish your hearts" (sterixai tas kardias) echoes the Septuagint's description of the righteous whose "heart is established/steadfast," unafraid. The image of an inwardly fixed, unshakable heart underlies Paul's prayer for hearts confirmed in holiness.

echoes.attribution: Catena, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wilson Pruitt / Wroot Press)

echoes.text: I saw in the night visions, and behold, there came with the clouds of the sky one like a son of man, and he came even to the ancient of days, and they brought him near before him. There was given him dominion, and glory, and a kingdom, that all the peoples, nations, and languages should serve him: his dominion is an everlasting dominion, which shall not pass away, and his kingdom that which shall not be destroyed.
echoes.note: Daniel sees 'one like a son of man' coming with the clouds of heaven, given dominion, glory, and a kingdom. Jesus' 'they will see the Son of Man coming in a cloud with power and great glory' is the climactic appropriation of this throne-vision, the most important OT reference in the discourse. Highest volume, recurrence, and coherence.

echoes.text: For the stars of the sky and its constellations will not give their light. The sun will be darkened in its going out, and the moon will not cause its light to shine.
echoes.note: In the Day-of-the-Lord oracle the stars, constellations, sun, and moon withhold their light. Jesus' 'signs in the sun, moon, and stars' draws directly on this prophetic darkening of the heavenly bodies. High coherence with the standard cosmic-collapse catalog.

echoes.text: All of the army of the sky will be dissolved. The sky will be rolled up like a scroll, and all its armies will fade away, as a leaf fades from off a vine or a fig tree.
echoes.note: The host of heaven rots away, the heavens roll up like a scroll, and all their host falls. Jesus' 'powers of the heavens will be shaken' echoes this dissolution of the celestial host on the day of judgment. Strong recurrence within the Day-of-the-Lord tradition.

echoes.text: The earth quakes before them. The heavens tremble. The sun and the moon are darkened, and the stars withdraw their shining.
echoes.note: Joel's day of the Lord: the earth quakes, the heavens tremble, sun and moon darken, the stars withdraw their shining. Jesus' combination of cosmic signs and shaken heavenly powers maps closely onto Joel's portrait. High coherence and recurrence.

echoes.text: I will show wonders in the heavens and in the earth: blood, fire, and pillars of smoke. The sun will be turned into darkness, and the moon into blood, before the great and terrible day of Yahweh comes.
echoes.note: Wonders in the heavens and on earth, the sun turned to darkness and moon to blood before the great and terrible Day. Jesus' celestial signs as harbingers of the coming day belong to this Joel sign-tradition, cited at Acts 2:19-20. Coherence reinforced by Lukan usage.

echoes.text: Ah, the uproar of many peoples, who roar like the roaring of the seas; and the rushing of nations, that rush like the rushing of mighty waters! The nations will rush like the rushing of many waters: but he will rebuke them, and they will flee far off, and will be chased like the chaff of the mountains before the wind, and like the whirling dust before the storm.
echoes.note: Isaiah likens the raging nations to the roaring of many waters, the tumult of the seas, before God rebukes them. Jesus' 'anxiety of nations, in perplexity for the roaring of the sea and the waves' fuses the nations' distress with the sea's roar exactly as Isaiah does. Strong conceptual coherence.

echoes.text: who stills the roaring of the seas, the roaring of their waves, and the turmoil of the nations.
echoes.note: God 'stills the roaring of the seas, the roaring of their waves, and the tumult of the peoples,' linking sea-roar and nations' tumult. Jesus' pairing of the roaring sea with the perplexity of nations echoes this psalmic juxtaposition. Coherence on the distinctive sea-and-nations parallel.

echoes.text: Therefore we won’t be afraid, though the earth changes, though the mountains are shaken into the heart of the seas; though its waters roar and are troubled, though the mountains tremble with their swelling. Selah.
echoes.note: Though the earth gives way, the mountains fall into the sea, and its waters roar and foam, the faithful need not fear. Jesus' roaring sea and shaken heavens amid which disciples lift up their heads in confidence mirror this psalm of cosmic upheaval and trust. Coherence with the tehom-chaos imagery.

echoes.text: For this is what Yahweh of Armies says: ‘Yet once, it is a little while, and I will shake the heavens, the earth, the sea, and the dry land;
echoes.note: God promises 'yet once more I will shake the heavens and the earth, the sea and the dry land,' and the kingdoms. Jesus' shaken 'powers of the heavens' draws on Haggai's eschatological cosmic shaking. Coherence with the shaking-of-creation motif.

echoes.text: The earth is utterly broken. The earth is torn apart. The earth is shaken violently. The earth will stagger like a drunken man, and will sway back and forth like a hammock. Its disobedience will be heavy on it, and it will fall and not rise again.
echoes.note: In the apocalypse of Isaiah the earth is utterly broken, staggering like a drunkard, its transgression heavy upon it. The men 'fainting for fear' before a reeling cosmos belongs to this Isaian universal-judgment scene. Coherence with the proto-apocalyptic dissolution.

echoes.text: Yahweh will be seen over them; and his arrow will go flash like lightning; and the Lord Yahweh will blow the trumpet, and will go with whirlwinds of the south.
echoes.note: The Lord appears over his people, his arrow goes forth like lightning, marching in the whirlwinds. The theophanic coming with power amid cosmic disturbance faintly colors Jesus' glorious Son-of-Man advent. Faint and atmospheric.

echoes.text: The grass withers, the flower fades; but the word of our God stands forever.”
echoes.note: Isaiah declares, 'the grass withers, the flower fades, but the word of our God will stand forever.' Jesus' 'heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will by no means pass away' applies this contrast of transient creation and abiding divine word to his own speech. High coherence on the enduring-word theme.

echoes.text: Lift up your eyes to the heavens, and look on the earth beneath; for the heavens shall vanish away like smoke, and the earth shall wax old like a garment; and those who dwell therein shall die in the same way: but my salvation shall be forever, and my righteousness shall not be abolished.
echoes.note: Isaiah: 'the heavens will vanish like smoke, the earth will wear out like a garment... but my salvation will be forever.' The passing of heaven and earth set against an everlasting divine word/salvation is exactly Jesus' antithesis. Strong recurrence within Isaiah of the perishing-cosmos vs. abiding-word motif.

echoes.text: Of old, you laid the foundation of the earth. The heavens are the work of your hands. They will perish, but you will endure. Yes, all of them will wear out like a garment. You will change them like a cloak, and they will be changed. But you are the same. Your years will have no end.
echoes.note: The heavens and earth perish and wear out like a garment, but God remains the same and his years have no end. Jesus' 'heaven and earth will pass away' draws on this psalmic contrast between the perishable creation and the unchanging God/word. Coherence with the creation-perishes tradition.

echoes.text: Don’t be afraid, you animals of the field; for the pastures of the wilderness spring up, for the tree bears its fruit. The fig tree and the vine yield their strength.
echoes.note: Joel's restoration: the fig tree and vine yield their fruit as a sign the land is renewed after the day of the Lord. Jesus' fig tree budding as a sign that the Kingdom is near may echo this prophetic use of the fig tree as harbinger. Faint thematic link to seasonal-sign imagery.

echoes.text: All of the army of the sky will be dissolved. The sky will be rolled up like a scroll, and all its armies will fade away, as a leaf fades from off a vine or a fig tree.
echoes.note: The heavens roll up like a scroll and the host falls like a leaf from the fig tree (LXX). The fig-tree image and the passing heavens cluster in Isaiah's judgment, faintly underlying Jesus' fig-tree parable juxtaposed with heaven and earth passing. Faint compositional echo.

echoes.text: Fear, the pit, and the snare, are on you who inhabitant the earth.
echoes.note: Isaiah's apocalypse: 'terror and the pit and the snare are upon you, O inhabitant of the earth.' Jesus' warning that the day will come 'like a snare on all those who dwell on the surface of all the earth' reproduces both the snare and the inhabitants-of-the-earth phrasing. High volume on the distinctive double image.

echoes.text: “Behold, I send my messenger, and he will prepare the way before me; and the Lord, whom you seek, will suddenly come to his temple; and the messenger of the covenant, whom you desire, behold, he comes!” says Yahweh of Armies. “But who can endure the day of his coming? And who will stand when he appears? For he is like a refiner’s fire, and like launderer’s soap;
echoes.note: The Lord will suddenly come to his temple, and who can stand (endure) the day of his coming? Jesus' call to be watchful so as to be able to 'stand before the Son of Man' on the suddenly-arriving day echoes Malachi's question of who can stand at the Lord's advent. Coherence with the standing-at-judgment motif.

echoes.text: I saw in the night visions, and behold, there came with the clouds of the sky one like a son of man, and he came even to the ancient of days, and they brought him near before him.
echoes.note: Standing 'before the Son of Man' recalls the Danielic court scene where the saints are vindicated before the one like a son of man given dominion. The closing exhortation ties the paraenesis back to Daniel 7, the discourse's controlling vision. Coherence by inclusio with 21:27.

echoes.text: He will be a sanctuary, but for both houses of Israel, he will be a trap and a snare for the inhabitants of Jerusalem. Many will stumble over it, fall, be broken, be snared, and be captured.”
echoes.note: The Lord becomes a snare and a trap to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and many stumble and are taken. The snare that suddenly catches the unprepared resonates with Jesus' sudden snare on the earth-dwellers. Faint recurrence of the snare-of-judgment image.

echoes.text: “For, behold, the day comes, it burns as a furnace; and all the proud, and all who work wickedness, will be stubble; and the day that comes will burn them up,” says Yahweh of Armies, “that it shall leave them neither root nor branch.
echoes.note: The day comes burning like an oven against the arrogant and evildoers. The sudden, inescapable arrival of 'that day' against the unwary colors Jesus' warning, though the imagery differs. Faint thematic link to the Day-of-the-Lord suddenness.

echoes.text: Who may ascend to Yahweh’s hill? Who may stand in his holy place? He who has clean hands and a pure heart; who has not lifted up his soul to falsehood, and has not sworn deceitfully. He shall receive a blessing from Yahweh, righteousness from the God of his salvation. This is the generation of those who seek Him, who seek your face—even Jacob. Selah.
echoes.note: The psalm asks who may stand in God's holy place, answering with the clean of hands and pure of heart. Jesus' exhortation to watchful, sober readiness so as to stand before the Son of Man evokes the worthiness-to-stand theme. Faint and contested.

echoes.text: Don’t be among ones drinking too much wine, or those who gorge themselves on meat: for the drunkard and the glutton shall become poor; and drowsiness clothes them in rags.
echoes.note: Wisdom warns against being among drunkards and gluttons, for drunkenness and carousing bring poverty and ruin. Jesus' caution that hearts not be weighed down by carousing and drunkenness draws on this sapiential warning against dissipation. Faint wisdom-tradition coloring.

registers.label: Spare
lines: The days are surely coming, says the Lord.
We lift up our souls and wait.
A righteous Branch will spring up for the land.
We lift up our souls and wait.
Stand up and raise your heads; your redemption draws near.
Come, let us worship the God who is coming. Amen.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: Look up. The night is wide and the stars are unsteady, and somewhere a green shoot is pushing through frozen ground.
Come, Lord Jesus, come.
Into our waiting, into the long dark of the year, God is doing a slow and certain thing.
Come, Lord Jesus, come.
A branch will grow from an old cut stump; what looked finished is not finished.
Come, Lord Jesus, come.
So lift up your heads, watch the horizon, lean toward the dawn.
Come, Lord Jesus, come. We are watching for you.

registers.label: Hybrid
lines: A green branch from an old stump — God is not finished.
Come, Lord Jesus, come.
We lift up our souls in the long dark.
Come, Lord Jesus, come.
Lift up your heads; redemption draws near.
Come, Lord Jesus, come. Amen.
